children: A key 'affordability' rate just touched its highest level since 2007
The U.S. dollar is getting a haven bid as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note tops 5%.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield touched the crucial 5% threshold on Monday, with oil prices marching higher, jitters about artificial intelligence growing and investors looking elsewhere for safety.

Known as the "affordability" yield, the 10-year rate BX:TMUBMUSD10Y briefly climbed as high as 5.011% Monday, hitting its highest intraday yield since July 19, 2007, when it reached 5.069%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
"It is a psychologically important level," said Brij Khurana, fixed-income portfolio manager at Wellington. Yields and bond prices move in opposite directions.

The continued sharp selloff in the $31.5 trillion Treasury market risks further increasing borrowing cost for households, businesses, the AI companies known as hyperscalers and the U.S. government. The federal budget deficit was recently pegged at nearly $2 trillion.

"You can already see [concern] among policymakers who are getting nervous about the level of yields," Khurana said. His view is that the Federal Reserve could risk losing control of long-dated 10-year and 30-year yields BX:TMUBMUSD30Y - which happened in the U.K. in 2022 - if U.S. central bankers opt not to raise interest rates at their meeting on Wednesday.
Khurana said he supports a "precautionary" hike, because the bond market has been behaving in a very nervous way.

The policy-sensitive 2-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD02Y was also pushing higher Monday to 4.66%, well above the 3.75% upper limit of the Fed's policy range. That signals traders are bracing for at least one Fed rate hike by the end of this year.

Inflation in the U.S. remains above 3%, well above the Fed's 2% yearly target. Oil prices also were surging again Monday as the Iran conflict intensified, lifting global crude prices (BRN00) to nearly $109 a barrel.

Stocks SPX DJIA COMP were lower Monday on concerns about the AI industry potentially hitting pause due to safety concerns. However, software stocks in the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF IGV were up 3.2%, according to FactSet.

The dollar also was finally seeing some haven support Monday. The ICE U.S. Dollar index DXY was up 0.5%, climbing against a basket of rival currencies, something the greenback has struggled to do during the summer selloff in the Treasury market.
